Chapter 11: The Ongoing Journey—Returning Again and Again.
You know, awakening isn’t just a single moment you experience and then check off your list. It’s really a lifelong journey—something we return to, over and over, in all sorts of ways. There’s no finish line where you suddenly “arrive” and everything’s complete. Every new day? It brings its own challenges, fresh opportunities, and gentle invitations to reconnect with that deep source of love inside us.
Picture a wise teacher nearing the end of their career. They look back on the many seasons of their life—times filled with certainty and others shadowed by doubt, moments of pure joy and stretches of real loss. Through it all, their practice stayed simple: returning, again and again, to the present moment. Listening to that quiet inner voice. Trusting in the wellspring of love that never runs dry.
A lot of people imagine spiritual growth as a straight line—always moving up. But in truth, it’s more like a spiral. We circle back to old lessons, but we see them differently each time. With every turn, we deepen our understanding. There’s a story in the book about someone who, after years of practice, found themselves facing the same fears and doubts they thought they’d left behind. At first, it felt discouraging—like all the progress had slipped away. But over time, they realized something important: every return was a new chance to dig deeper, to love more openly, to trust even more.
This journey isn’t really about perfection. It’s about presence. It’s about showing up, day after day, with an open heart—even when it’s hard. So many of us judge ourselves for not being “spiritual enough,” or for not living up to our ideals. But here’s something to remember: the only real failure is to stop trying—to close your heart, or to give up on love.
So, as the book comes to a close, here’s the invitation: keep returning, no matter how often you stumble or how far you feel you’ve strayed. That source of love? It’s always waiting, ready to welcome you home.
